headline: High: open-webui can share files, MCP, and broad egress with opik, creating default-path data leakage and cascading misinterpretation risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest local files, mounted volumes, MCP, and OpenAPI tool outputs, so attacker-controlled content can reach its prompt/tool pipeline. opik exposes a REST API and broad egress, so if its outputs are fed into open-webui or vice versa, instruction-like content could be relayed. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF opik outputs are copied into open-webui chats or files without provenance labels
IF open-webui MCP/OpenAPI tool results are rendered as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable or restrict MCP/OpenAPI tools for untrusted sources
Add a provenance banner to all opik-generated text before import
Use a read-only staging folder for any shared files
Train operators to treat tool output as data, not instructions
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly touches prompts, chat messages, documents, notes, calendar events, artifacts, persistent memory, usage analytics, model evaluation data, files, and API keys, and it can access local files and mounted volumes. opik has broad network egress and a REST API, so if it receives any of that shared content, leakage to a third party is plausible. Because the pairwise workspace boundary is undocumented, uncertainty favors high.
conditions: IF open-webui and opik share any workspace, export path, or API payload containing files or API keys
IF opik forwards received content to an external service or backend
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove API keys and secrets from any shared folder
Turn off file ingestion for shared sessions
Review outbound destinations for opik REST traffic
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui supports persistent shared web app sessions, Redis-backed shared state, multiple instances, and file writes, while opik exposes a REST API and broad egress. That creates overlapping mutable surfaces if both are pointed at the same resources, even though opik's write scope is not documented here. The conflict is plausible in default deployments, but not proven high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared directory, session store, or API-backed resource
IF open-webui multi-worker sessions and opik REST actions target the same mutable object
mitigations: Assign separate directories and databases per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use a single writer for any shared resource
Check for lock support before enabling multi-instance mode
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking or transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can produce tool outputs, files, and persistent memory that opik may ingest through its REST API or evaluation workflows. If opik treats those outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream evaluation or reporting. There is no evidence of verification gates between them, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF opik consumes open-webui outputs without an explicit verification step
IF open-webui-generated artifacts are used as ground truth in opik workflows
mitigations: Insert a human review step before opik ingests outputs
Mark open-webui outputs as untrusted in metadata
Compare outputs against source documents before evaluation
Limit opik to read-only analysis of exported artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated verification and citation checks

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui handles API keys, documents, calendar events, and persistent memory, while opik is an open-source evaluation/observability system with only a REST API documented here and no stated residency or retention controls. If regulated data from open-webui is sent into opik, retention or residency mismatches are possible. The evidence is incomplete, so medium is appropriate rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents, calendar events, or API keys from open-webui are exported into opik
IF opik retention or hosting differs from the source data's residency requirements
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from any opik export
Redact secrets before transfer
Document retention settings for both systems
Confirm hosting region before enabling sync
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing and retention enforcement
